correctness.rationale: Diagonal translation kills all frequencies but the q³ with total character zero. For the remaining ones, sum over all equality partitions with Möbius weights (+1,−1,+2,+1,−6) for block-size types 1111,211,31,22,4. A block contributes q iff its character sum is zero, so four zero coordinates give the injective count, two give −q(q−2)(q−3), one gives 2q(q−3) and no zeros give q²P−6q for P opposite perfect pairings. The zero-coordinate multiplicities are 1, 6(q−1) and 4(q−1)(q−2). Among nonzero balanced tuples, the total q³−4q²+6q−3 follows by inclusion–exclusion. Three pairings mean four copies of a nonzero involution; exactly two mean permutations of (a,a,−a,−a) with a≠−a, counted as 6(q−t)/2. Counting incidences of the three patterns yields M₁=3(q−1)²−2M₂−3M₃ and M₀ by subtraction, which are exactly the claimed polynomials. Only P=1 can introduce a balanced zero, at q=6; the abelian group of order six is cyclic, t=2, so there are 48 such zeros, rank 168. The full rank on the translation-invariant subspace elsewhere gives the range equality. For q>4, 3q(q−2) is distinct from every other level, and at q=4 it also includes the trivial character, giving multiplicity t instead of t−1. The sign convention merely inverts frequencies. Reduce roots of unity to a finite field containing an element of the group's exponent order, with prime >2q(q−1)(q−2)(q−3), so each integer coefficient proved above is uniquely recovered without rounding. These tests check instances; the proof is valid for all finite abelian groups of order at least four with unnormalized counting convolution.
